title: a-ticket-has-one-status-and-one-reader
owner: operator_inbox is a tool with users (Law 6): the codemother dashboard and the harbor_master map consume its reader; codemother owns the care of the code (ruling 2026-09-06). CC/Opus builds. harbor_master's charter changes wording and its owner (cairn device) gates that write.
intention: A ticket has one status, its cursor, and the three operator reports (operator inbox, codemother dashboard, harbor_master map) read it through one reader in operator_inbox and show it with one label, so the same ticket carries the same status wherever it appears and the reports differ only by filter and format.
why: Akien 2026-09-06 evening, reading `akienupdate`: 'one of these reports are showing apparently different statuses per item' — then, once the cause was measured: 'the three reports should show more or less the same data, depending on filters and formats. they're kinda venn diagrams. so whatever's in the way of that's a bug.' and 'for a given ticket that appers in all the places, i should see the same status. it has one status.' The lived symptom: the operator opens his three reports every session and the same ticket wears two statuses on one page, the inbox header contradicts its own listing, and three components appear as stages that do not exist.
traces_to: Law 1 (three readers re-derive one settled answer; the label is derived once); Law 7 (the map collapsed a log's last entry into a status and turned prose into groups silently; a diagnostic surface is loud instead); Law 5 (history.json is the record of what is under way, not the status; the ticket's cursor is the status); CP4 (the operator reads one status, not three translations of it). Ideas 2026-09-06-the-three-reports-should-show-more-or and 2026-09-06-for-a-given-ticket-that-appers-in (Akien: 'for a given ticket that appers in all the places, i should see the same status. it has one status.'). Neighbour: a705346aa75c operator-show-reaches-all-inbox-items (same tool, the show_artifact path, at PROVEME:waiting; distinct seam).
falsifier: DONE when, on this box, after `akienupdate`: (1) every ticket id that appears in any of the three reports carries one status token, byte-identical in every report where it appears, asserted by test_one_status_everywhere.py over the live commons and over a fixture; (2) the inbox header's ticket counts sum to its own TICKETS line and the word 'other' does not appear; (3) grep over inbox.py, dashboard.py, register.py, device.py finds exactly one function deriving a label from a cursor, in operator_inbox, and no private cursor regex or token scan outside transitions.parse_workflow; (4) the harbor map has no row without a date and a ticket id, and no group name outside the stage vocabulary of transitions; (5) all 39 non-terminal tickets carry owning_intention (0 unassigned in the component lane); (6) cc, diagnostic_inspector, system_rackmount, sudo_relay, charter appear on the map only as a finding line naming the prose standing, or not at all; (7) after a clearance crossing, `show map` before reconcile shows the ticket's file cursor, not the bare target. Horizon: the Opus build session. WRONG INTENT if history.json is made to carry the cursor (it is the crossing log; the ticket is the status), or if a fourth reader appears anywhere, or if a report starts storing what it shows.

questions.a: Three named and measured. (1) The ticket's cursor is the one status: transitions.pickup writes ':waiting' into the ticket string and clearance appends the crossing to history.json; the cursor is where the phase lives, the history is where the crossing lives. (2) Nothing but the harbor map and device.py:79's cache patch reads a component's in-port standing (grep across cairn, bin, skills: register is imported only by device.py). (3) Every non-terminal ticket can carry an owning_intention: 32 do; of the 7 that do not, 728d393d70ed is a concept-piece and 'CairnCommons' is the owning value 6 tickets already use; the other 6 name their component in their own text (every-device-has-a-presence → bus; the-deposit-rides-the-read → chart; skills-migrate-one-blow → skill_block; probescan → system_rackmount; superclaude-starts-itself → sudo_relay/rescue; logger-for-bash → bin). The builder confirms each from the ticket, not from this list.

Two points asserted wrapped that were not. (a) The crossing-notification cache patch (device.py:70-82) is a FOURTH place a status is derived, missed in the first read; it writes the bare target and is folded in as step (d). (b) The dashboard's 'adjudication(s)' count reads data['lap'], a different datum from the review queue (data['adjudications']); the word survived the review-queue rewrite while the meaning moved. The cast renames the line rather than deleting the datum: the lap count stays if read_lap still measures something (builder checks read_lap's source; if it reads the dissolved adjudications dir and is always 0, delete it and its reader in the same act).

Carried from /intent: one status token per ticket id across the three reports (proof over fixture and live); inbox header sums to its listing with no 'other'; exactly one label function and no private cursor parser outside transitions; no undated or id-less map row and no group outside the stage vocabulary; 0 unassigned in the component lane; prose standings surface as a finding line only; the cache patch shows the file cursor before reconcile. Horizon: the Opus build session. Wrong-intent teeth: history.json made to carry the cursor; a fourth reader; a report that stores.

Consulted the lab (recompiled 2026-09-06). harbor_master charter + test_harbor_register.py: in-port standing == project(history).cursor. Same why on both sides (an index must not compute a rival record); dissolves once 'the boat's own record' names the ticket rather than the log. A charter change, flagged at Akien's gate. a705346aa75c operator-show-reaches-all-inbox-items: same tool, different seam (show_artifact), no overlap in lines. Ruling 2026-09-06-codemother-owns-the-care-of-the-code: the dashboard is codemother's face and stays codemother's; the reader is a tool with users (Law 6), which is why it lives in operator_inbox and both codemother and harbor_master import it without a cross-device import (memory no-cross-device-imports covers devices, not tools). Law 5: honored, history.json is untouched and stays the record of what is under way.

A Haiku-level builder needs: (a) WHERE — cairn/tools/operator_inbox/inbox.py: `read_tickets` returns {'records': [ {id, title, date, cursor, label, owning_component, source} ], 'by_label': {label: [ids]}, 'total_not_done'}; cursor via `from cairn.tools.base.transitions import parse_workflow` (wf.path[wf.cursor] plus ':'+wf.phase when phase); `status_label(cursor)` = base stage, plus ':waiting' when phase is waiting, WATCHME object stripped; owning_component = owning_intention with 'cairn/cairn/' prefix and '/intention+why.json' suffix removed, else 'unassigned'. Delete `_cursor`. Header summary (inbox.py:295-308) iterates by_label in transitions' priority order; no 'other'. (b) cairn/devices/codemother/dashboard.py: delete `_count_done`, `_read_tickets_with_detail`; `_format_atom` takes a record and prints record['label'] verbatim; done counts come from a `read_done_tickets` in inbox.py (terminal cursors) so the dashboard globs nothing; lines 124-126 become one review-queue line and one email line. (c) cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/register.py: `_open_boats` = read_tickets records with berth 'open'; `_berthed_boats` returns the same records keyed by owning_component with berth 'in_port' (a component is a berth, the boats at it are its tickets) and a 'findings' list of components whose history.json last standing is not in transitions' vocabulary; delete `_CURSOR_RE`. device.py `_render_fleet_map`: open lane grouped by label in _PRIORITY_ORDER, in-port lane grouped by component with each ticket's label beside it, findings printed as 'FINDING: <component> history standing is prose: <first 60 chars>'; delete `_standing_short`, use record['label']; `_format_boat` prints date, label, full 12-char id, title for every row. device.py:70-82: on a crossing, reload the named ticket file and set standing = its label. (d) THE TICKET PATCHES — add owning_intention to 0146df77dae1, 12c293481037, 18693659d16b, 59a66e1c4a1a, 728d393d70ed ('CairnCommons'), 835af7f398ce, 854db29ffddf, each from the ticket's own text; commit with the ticket id in the message. (e) PROOFS — new cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/test_one_status_everywhere.py: build a tickets fixture in a tmp dir (five tickets across TICKETME:waiting, PROVEME:waiting, WATCHME(x):waiting, WATCHME(x), PROVED) plus one history.json fixture with a prose standing; render inbox, dashboard, map over it (tickets_dir kwargs exist on all three readers; the map takes cairn_root + tickets_dir); assert per-id status token identical, header sums, no 'other', finding line present, PROVED absent from all three under the open filter; then run once over the live commons. Reseal test_operator_inbox.py, test_fleet_map.py, test_harbor_register.py (rewrite its in-port tooth to 'standing == the ticket's label'). (f) CHARTER — harbor_master/intention+why.json: in-port lane wording changes to 'the open tickets berthed at each component'; run cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh in the same commit. (g) ORDER — (a) with its proof teeth, then (b), then (c), then (d), then (e) live run, then (f). (h) DON'TS — no write to history.json; no new glob of tickets/ anywhere; no cursor regex outside transitions; do not drop the map's in-port lane (it is a format Akien keeps); do not touch show_artifact (a705346aa75c owns it).

constraints: history.json is never written here and never made to carry a cursor: it is the crossing log (Law 5); the ticket's cursor is the status.
One reader, in operator_inbox; no other module globs tickets/ or parses a cursor outside transitions.parse_workflow.
The harbor map keeps its in-port lane as a FORMAT (tickets grouped by owning component); it loses its second population, not its lane.
show_artifact is a705346aa75c's seam and is not touched.
Prose standings in a component's history.json surface as a loud finding line on the map (Law 7), never as a group and never silently dropped.
how: MEASURED 2026-09-06 against `akienupdate` (CairnCommons/AkienInbox.txt, AkienDashboard.txt, AkienHMMap.txt) and the code at cairn 35a915b. Three readers glob CairnCommons/tickets/*.json and each derives its own status label: inbox.py `read_tickets` + `_cursor` (token scan); dashboard.py `_read_tickets_with_detail` + `_count_done` + `_format_atom` (re-globs, re-derives base/waiting); harbor_master/register.py `_open_boats` (its own `_CURSOR_RE`) + device.py `_standing_short`. Four divergences follow. (1) The inbox header says '39 tickets (other 39)' while its own TICKETS line says 'TICKETME:waiting (8) | PROVEME:waiting (19) | WATCHME (12)': inbox.py:297-304 buckets by bare stage and every cursor now carries ':waiting'. (2) The harbor map shows the bus as `PROVEME` (in-port row, id 'bus', no date, no title) and as `87a7f1c7ae21 PROVEME:waiting` (open row): `_berthed_boats` reads the LAST ENTRY of the component's history.json (the crossing log) and presents it as a status; 13 components show this way. (3) Three components whose last history standing is prose become groups on the map: 'Device' (cc), 'BERTHED' (diagnostic_inspector), 'diagnostic' (system_rackmount); sudo_relay and charter start with 'PROVED —' and land right by luck. Started at cb33ce6 (2026-09-04) which collapsed the map's two lanes into one list; test_fleet_map.py asserts only that 'open' and one id appear in the text. (4) device.py:70-82 patches the fleet cache on a crossing notification with standing=target (e.g. 'PROVEME'), never the ticket's cursor after the summons ('PROVEME:waiting'), so the cached map drifts from the ticket file until reconcile. Also: dashboard prints the review queue count under two names ('awaiting review' and 'adjudication(s)' from the lap) and the email count twice ('lost email', 'EMAIL: 0 unresolved'). THE SEAM, in cairn/tools/operator_inbox (a tool; dashboard already imports it): (a) inbox.py `read_tickets` returns per-ticket records {id, title, date, cursor, label, owning_component, source} where cursor comes from `transitions.parse_workflow` (the one parser; delete `_cursor`'s token scan and register's `_CURSOR_RE`) and `label = status_label(cursor)` is THE display label (base, or base:waiting; WATCHME keeps its object out of the label); the header summary sums by label so 'other' cannot appear. (b) dashboard.py deletes `_read_tickets_with_detail`, `_count_done`, `_format_atom`'s re-derivation and formats the records; one review-queue line, one email line; the word 'adjudication' goes. (c) register.py `_open_boats` calls `read_tickets`; `_berthed_boats` stops reading a status from history.json: the in-port lane becomes the same open tickets grouped by owning_component (the harbor's format of the same set), and a component whose history.json last standing is not a vocabulary stage is reported as one loud finding line on the map (Law 7), never a group. history.json stays the crossing log for clearance; nothing writes it here. (d) device.py's crossing patch re-reads the ticket's cursor from the file it names instead of writing target. (e) The 7 non-terminal tickets with no owning_intention (0146df77dae1, 12c293481037, 18693659d16b, 59a66e1c4a1a, 728d393d70ed, 835af7f398ce, 854db29ffddf) are patched to carry one, so the component lane has no 'unassigned' bucket. (f) One proof, test_one_status_everywhere.py, renders all three over one tickets fixture and asserts the status token beside every ticket id is identical across the three, the inbox header sums equal its listing, and a prose-standing history yields a finding line. The four touched proofs reseal.

intent.what: A ticket has one status, its cursor, and the three operator reports (operator inbox, codemother dashboard, harbor_master map) read it through one reader in operator_inbox and show it with one label, so the same ticket carries the same status wherever it appears and the reports differ only by filter and format.

challenge.better_approach: Delete the harbor map and keep the dashboard, since the map's open lane is now byte-identical to the dashboard's ticket section. Rejected: the harbor master is the crossing authority and its map is the fleet by berth (which boat at which component), a format the dashboard does not have; Akien's words are 'depending on filters and formats', so the map keeps its format and loses its second population. Another: fix each report in place. Rejected: three fixes of one label is Law 1's defect restated; the divergences measured today are all the same reader written three times.
challenge.prior_art: dashboard.py already imports read_tickets from operator_inbox (cb33ce6): the seam is the direction the code was already going; transitions.parse_workflow (the one parser, returns cursor + phase); register.py's own docstring 'an index, not a rival record' and test_harbor_register.py's tooth that in-port standing is byte-equal to project(history).cursor, which this cast rewrites to 'byte-equal to the ticket's cursor'; register.py's `HARBOR REGISTER` printer that still prints the two lanes apart.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That every non-terminal ticket can be given an owning component. Measured: 32 of 39 have one, 7 do not; 6 tickets already use 'CairnCommons' as owning_intention for concept-pieces, so 728d393d70ed has a legal home and the other 6 name their component in their own prose. Second: that a component's in-port standing is not read by anything but the map. device.py:79 patches it on a crossing notification; nothing else reads it (grep). Third: that the harbor_master charter's wording 'in-port boats: every component carrying a history.json' is a translation, not the spec; Akien's 'it has one status' is the spec, so the charter's in-port lane changes meaning and the recompile gate runs.
challenge.real_collision: harbor_master's charter and test_harbor_register.py define in-port standing as project(history).cursor. Why of that side: an index must not compute a rival to the boat's own record. Why of this side: the boat's own record IS the ticket's cursor; history.json is the log of its crossings. They are the same why; the collision dissolves once 'the boat's own record' names the ticket. Recorded as a distinction, and flagged at Akien's gate because it changes a charter. No Law collides.

why_beneath_the_why: Three surfaces each re-derived 'what is this ticket's status' because no one function answered it; the answer was settled the day transitions.parse_workflow was written, and re-deriving a settled answer is Law 1's defect. The divergences are what the re-derivation cost.
